Sundaland.question: In addition to the _____ and the islands of Borneo, Java, and Sumatra, it includes the Java Sea, the Gulf of Thailand, and portions of the South China Sea
Sundaland.fact: == Extent == The area of Sundaland encompasses the Sunda Shelf, a tectonically stable extension of Southeast Asia's continental shelf that was exposed during glacial periods of the last 2 million years.  It is also roughly coterminous with the Sunda plate.  The extent of the Sunda Shelf is approximately equal to the 120-meter isobath. Sundaland.subject: Environment & Ecology
Sundaland.question: The area of exposed land in Sundaland has fluctuated considerably during the past recent _____ years; the modern land area is approximately half of its maximum extent
Sundaland.fact: The extent of the Sunda Shelf is approximately equal to the 120-meter isobath.  In addition to the Malay Peninsula and the islands of Borneo, Java, and Sumatra, it includes the Java Sea, the Gulf of Thailand, and portions of the South China Sea.  In total, the area of Sundaland is approximately 1,800,000 km2.  The area of exposed land in Sundaland has fluctuated considerably during the past recent 2 million years; the modern land area is approximately half of its maximum extent.  The western and southern borders of Sundaland are clearly marked by the deeper waters of the Sunda Trench – some of the deepest in the world – and the Indian Ocean.  The eastern boundary of Sundaland is the Wallace Line, identified by Alfred Russel Wallace as the eastern boundary of the range of Asia's land mammal fauna, and thus the boundary of the Indomalayan and Australasian realms.  The islands east of the Wallace line are known as Wallacea, a separate biogeographical region that is considered part of Australasia

Sundaland.subject: Environment & Ecology
Sundaland.question: The fish is now found in the _____ on the island of Borneo, and in the Musi and Batanghari rivers in Sumatra
Sundaland.fact: As a result, the modern islands of Sundaland are home to many Asian mammals including elephants, monkeys, apes, tigers, tapirs, and rhinoceros.  The flooding of Sundaland separated species that had once shared the same environment.  One example is the river threadfin (Polydactylus macrophthalmus, Bleeker 1858), which once thrived in a river system now called "North Sunda River" or "Molengraaff river".  The fish is now found in the Kapuas River on the island of Borneo, and in the Musi and Batanghari rivers in Sumatra.  Selective pressure (in some cases resulting in extinction) has operated differently on each of the islands of Sundaland, and as a consequence, a different assemblage of mammals is found on each island.  However, the current species assemblage on each island is not simply a subset of a universal Sundaland or Asian fauna, as the species that inhabited Sundaland before flooding did not all have ranges encompassing the entire Sunda Shelf.  Island area and number of terrestrial mammal species are related, with the largest islands of Sundaland (Borneo and Sumatra) having the highest diversity

Sundaland.subject: Environment & Ecology
Sundaland.question: Snow was found much lower than at present (approximately 1,000 meters lower) and there is evidence that glaciers existed on Borneo and _____ around 10,000 years before present
Sundaland.fact: The presence of fossil coral reefs dating to the late Miocene and early Pliocene suggests that, as the Indian monsoon grew more intense, seasonality increased in some portions of Sundaland during these epochs.  Palynological evidence from Sumatra suggests that temperatures were cooler during the late Pleistocene; mean annual temperatures at high elevation sites may have been as much as 5 °C cooler than present.  Most recent research agrees that Indo-Pacific sea surface temperatures were at most 2-3 °C lower during the Last Glacial Maximum.  Snow was found much lower than at present (approximately 1,000 meters lower) and there is evidence that glaciers existed on Borneo and Sumatra around 10,000 years before present.  However, debate continues on how precipitation regimes changed throughout the Quaternary.  Some authors argue that rainfall decreased with the area of ocean available for evaporation as sea levels fell with ice sheet expansion.  Others posit that changes in precipitation have been minimal and an increase in land area in the Sunda Shelf alone (due to lowered sea level) is not enough to decrease precipitation in the region

Wars of the Roses.fact: The Black Prince had one surviving son, Richard, who had a claim to the throne based upon the principle that the son of the heir apparent had priority in the line of succession over his uncles. However, Richard was a minor, and his uncles were politically powerful and ambitious, so there was considerable uncertainty within the realm over who should inherit the throne.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Ultimately, _____ III was succeeded by his grandson who was crowned Richard II at just 10 years old
Wars of the Roses.fact: Edward III was survived by three sons with claims to the throne: John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster; Edmund of Langley, 1st Duke of York; and Thomas of Woodstock, 1st Duke of Gloucester. Ultimately, Edward III was succeeded by his grandson who was crowned Richard II at just 10 years old.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Lionel's only child _____ married into the Mortimer family and had a son, Roger Mortimer, who technically would have the best legal claim of succession
Wars of the Roses.fact: Lionel's only child Philippa married into the Mortimer family and had a son, Roger Mortimer, who technically would have the best legal claim of succession.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: England then faced various problems, most notably the _____' War
Wars of the Roses.fact: England then faced various problems, most notably the Hundred Years' War. Less warlike than either his father or grandfather, he sought to bring an end to the Hundred Years' War.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: A major challenge of the reign was the Peasants' Revolt in _____, and the young king played a central part in the successful suppression of this crisis
Wars of the Roses.fact: A major challenge of the reign was the Peasants' Revolt in 1381, and the young king played a central part in the successful suppression of this crisis.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: A firm believer in the royal prerogative, _____ restrained the power of the aristocracy and relied on a private retinue for military protection instead
Wars of the Roses.fact: A firm believer in the royal prerogative, Richard restrained the power of the aristocracy and relied on a private retinue for military protection instead. Richard's reign was tumultuous, marked by increasing dissension between the monarch and several of the most powerful nobles.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Richard ruled without a regency council despite his young age in order to exclude his uncle, John of Gaunt the Duke of _____, from wielding legitimate power
Wars of the Roses.fact: Richard ruled without a regency council despite his young age in order to exclude his uncle, John of Gaunt the Duke of Lancaster, from wielding legitimate power.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The king's dependence on a small number of courtiers caused discontent among the influential, and in _____ control of government was taken over by a group of aristocrats known as the Lords Appellant
Wars of the Roses.fact: The king's dependence on a small number of courtiers caused discontent among the influential, and in 1387 control of government was taken over by a group of aristocrats called the Lords Appellant.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: By 1389 _____ had regained control, and for the next eight years governed in relative harmony with his former opponents
Wars of the Roses.fact: Unpopular taxes which funded unsuccessful military expeditions in Europe triggered the Peasant's Revolt in 1381, and Parliament's refusal to cooperate with the king's unpopular Lord Chancellor, Michael de la Pole, created a political crisis that seriously threatened to dethrone Richard. Richard had repeatedly switched his choice of heir throughout his reign to keep his political enemies at bay.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In France, much of the territory conquered by Edward III had been lost, leading to the Truce of Leulinghem with Charles VI in July _____
Wars of the Roses.fact: By 1389 Richard had regained control, and for the next eight years governed in relative harmony with his former opponents. In France, much of the territory conquered by Edward III had been lost, leading to the Truce of Leulinghem with Charles VI in July 1389.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The peace proposal, which would effectively have made _____ a client kingdom of France, was derided and rejected by Parliament, which was predominately controlled by the knights fighting the war
Wars of the Roses.fact: The peace proposal, which would effectively have made England a client kingdom of France, was derided and rejected by Parliament, which was predominately controlled by the knights fighting the war.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Richard decided to negotiate a de facto peace directly with _____ without seeking Parliament's approval and agreed to marry his six-year-old daughter, Isabella of Valois
Wars of the Roses.fact: In France, much of the territory conquered by Edward III had been lost, leading to the Truce of Leulinghem with Charles VI in July 1389. Richard decided to negotiate a de facto peace directly with Charles without seeking Parliament's approval and agreed to marry his six-year-old daughter, Isabella of Valois.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In 1397, he took his revenge on the _____, many of whom were executed or exiled
Wars of the Roses.fact: In 1397, he took his revenge on the Appellants, many of whom were executed or exiled.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The next two years have been described by historians as _____'s "tyranny"
Wars of the Roses.fact: Richard decided to negotiate a de facto peace directly with Charles without seeking Parliament's approval and agreed to marry his six-year-old daughter, Isabella of Valois. Richard used the interim peace to punish his political rivals.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In May _____, Richard left England for a military expedition in Ireland, giving Bolingbroke the opportunity to return to England
Wars of the Roses.fact: In May 1399, Richard left England for a military expedition in Ireland, giving Bolingbroke the opportunity to return to England. Henry invaded England in June 1399 with a small force that quickly grew in numbers, meeting little resistance.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry invaded England in June _____ with a small force that quickly grew in numbers, meeting little resistance
Wars of the Roses.fact: In May 1399, Richard left England for a military expedition in Ireland, giving Bolingbroke the opportunity to return to England. Henry invaded England in June 1399 with a small force that quickly grew in numbers, meeting little resistance.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: With the support of much of the disaffected nobility, _____ deposed Richard and was crowned as Henry IV, the first Lancastrian monarch
Wars of the Roses.fact: In May 1399, Richard left England for a military expedition in Ireland, giving Bolingbroke the opportunity to return to England. With the support of much of the disaffected nobility, Bolingbroke deposed Richard and was crowned as Henry IV, the first Lancastrian monarch.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Modern historians do not accept this interpretation, while not exonerating _____ from responsibility for his own deposition
Wars of the Roses.fact: With the support of much of the disaffected nobility, Bolingbroke deposed Richard and was crowned as Henry IV, the first Lancastrian monarch. Richard is thought to have been starved to death in captivity, although questions remain regarding his final fate.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The attempt failed, all four conspirators were executed, and _____ died shortly thereafter "by means unknown" in Pontefract Castle
Wars of the Roses.fact: Modern historians do not accept this interpretation, while not exonerating Richard from responsibility for his own deposition. Most authorities agree that Richard's policies were not unrealistic or even entirely unprecedented, but that the way in which he carried them out was unacceptable to the political establishment, leading to his downfall.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Glyndŵr's rebellion would outlast Henry's reign, and would not end until _____
Wars of the Roses.fact: Glyndŵr's rebellion would outlast Henry's reign, and would not end until 1415.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The first challenge was defeated at Shrewsbury in _____ and Worcester was executed, while a second attempt failed at Bramham Moor in 1408, at which Northumberland was killed
Wars of the Roses.fact: The first challenge was defeated at Shrewsbury in 1403 and Worcester was executed, while a second attempt failed at Bramham Moor in 1408, at which Northumberland was killed.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: While not plagued by constant rebellions as his father's reign was, Henry V faced a major challenge to his authority on the eve of his expedition to France in the form of the _____
Wars of the Roses.fact: While not plagued by constant rebellions as his father's reign was, Henry V faced a major challenge to his authority on the eve of his expedition to France in the form of the Southampton Plot.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: This was led by _____, Henry, Baron Scrope, and Richard of Conisburgh, the latter of whom was the second son of Edmund of Langley the 1st Duke of York
Wars of the Roses.fact: This was led by Sir Thomas Grey, Henry, Baron Scrope, and Richard of Conisburgh, the latter of whom was the second son of Edmund of Langley the 1st Duke of York.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: They intended to replace Henry with the young _____, Richard of Conisburgh's brother-in-law, who was a great-great-grandson of Edward III and at one time the heir presumptive to Richard II
Wars of the Roses.fact: They intended to replace Henry with the young Edmund Mortimer, Richard of Conisburgh's brother-in-law, who was a great-great-grandson of Edward III and at one time the heir presumptive to Richard II.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Mortimer remained loyal and informed _____ of the plot, who had all three ringleaders executed
Wars of the Roses.fact: While not plagued by constant rebellions as his father's reign was, Henry V faced a major challenge to his authority on the eve of his expedition to France in the form of the Southampton Plot. This was led by Sir Thomas Grey, Henry, Baron Scrope, and Richard of Conisburgh, the latter of whom was the second son of Edmund of Langley the 1st Duke of York.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry captured _____ on 22 September and inflicted a decisive defeat on the French at Agincourt on 25 October which wiped out a significant part of the French nobility
Wars of the Roses.fact: Henry captured Harfleur on 22 September and inflicted a decisive defeat on the French at Agincourt on 25 October which wiped out a significant part of the French nobility.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Agincourt and Henry's subsequent campaigns firmly entrenched the legitimacy of the _____ monarchy and Henry's pursuit of his claims on the French throne
Wars of the Roses.fact: Agincourt and Henry's subsequent campaigns firmly entrenched the legitimacy of the Lancastrian monarchy and Henry's pursuit of his claims on the French throne.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In _____, Henry and Charles VI of France signed the Treaty of Troyes
Wars of the Roses.fact: In 1420, Henry and Charles VI of France signed the Treaty of Troyes.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The treaty disinherited the _____ from the line of succession, married Charles' daughter Catherine of Valois to Henry, and acknowledged their future sons as legitimate successors to the French throne
Wars of the Roses.fact: The treaty disinherited the French Dauphin Charles from the line of succession, married Charles' daughter Catherine of Valois to Henry, and acknowledged their future sons as legitimate successors to the French throne.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Richard of York, the son of Richard of _____, was four years old when his father was executed
Wars of the Roses.fact: Richard of York, the son of Richard of Conisburgh, was four years old when his father was executed.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: As his paternal uncle, _____, 2nd Duke of York, had died at Agincourt without issue, Henry permitted Richard of York to inherit the title and lands of the Duchy of York
Wars of the Roses.fact: As his paternal uncle, Edward, 2nd Duke of York, had died at Agincourt without issue, Henry permitted Richard of York to inherit the title and lands of the Duchy of York.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: When Edmund Mortimer died childless in _____, Richard of York also inherited the Earldom of March and Mortimer's claim to the throne through his late mother, Edmund Mortimer's sister
Wars of the Roses.fact: When Edmund Mortimer died childless in 1425, Richard of York also inherited the Earldom of March and Mortimer's claim to the throne through his late mother, Edmund Mortimer's sister.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry, who himself had three younger brothers and had recently married _____, did not doubt that the Lancastrian claim on the crown was secure
Wars of the Roses.fact: Henry, who himself had three younger brothers and had recently married Catherine, did not doubt that the Lancastrian claim on the crown was secure. On 6 December 1421, Catherine gave birth to a son, Henry.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The following year, _____ V died of dysentery, and his son ascended to the throne at just nine months old
Wars of the Roses.fact: Henry, who himself had three younger brothers and had recently married Catherine, did not doubt that the Lancastrian claim on the crown was secure. On 6 December 1421, Catherine gave birth to a son, Henry.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: On 6 December _____, Catherine gave birth to a son, Henry
Wars of the Roses.fact: On 6 December 1421, Catherine gave birth to a son, Henry.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry V's younger brothers produced no surviving legitimate heirs, leaving only the _____ family as alternative Lancastrian successors
Wars of the Roses.fact: Henry V's younger brothers produced no surviving legitimate heirs, leaving only the Beaufort family as alternative Lancastrian successors. His younger surviving paternal uncle, Humphrey, Duke of Gloucester, sought to be named Lord Protector until Henry came of age, and deliberately courted the popularity of the common people for his own ends, but was opposed by his half-uncle, Cardinal Henry Beaufort.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: As Richard of _____ grew into maturity and Henry VI's rule deteriorated, York's claim to the throne became more attractive
Wars of the Roses.fact: As Richard of York grew into maturity and Henry VI's rule deteriorated, York's claim to the throne became more attractive.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry was formally crowned as Henry VI, aged 7, shortly thereafter on 6 _____ in response to the coronation of Charles
Wars of the Roses.fact: Henry was formally crowned as Henry VI, aged 7, shortly thereafter on 6 November in response to the coronation of Charles.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry came of age in _____ at age sixteen
Wars of the Roses.fact: Henry came of age in 1437 at age sixteen.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Suffolk was opposed by _____ and the rising Richard of York, both of whom favoured a continued prosecution of a military solution against France
Wars of the Roses.fact: Suffolk was opposed by Gloucester and the rising Richard of York, both of whom favoured a continued prosecution of a military solution against France. Suffolk and the Beaufort family frequently received large grants of money, land, and important government and military positions from the king, who preferred their less hawkish inclinations, redirecting much-needed resources away from Richard and Gloucester's campaigns in France, leading to Richard developing a bitter resentment for the Beauforts.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Suffolk continued to increase his influence at court as the principal architect of the Treaty of Tours in _____ to broker peace between England and France
Wars of the Roses.fact: Suffolk continued to increase his influence at court as the principal architect of the Treaty of Tours in 1444 to broker peace between England and France.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Two years later in _____, Suffolk succeeded in having Gloucester arrested for treason
Wars of the Roses.fact: Two years later in 1447, Suffolk succeeded in having Gloucester arrested for treason.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Gloucester died while awaiting trial, with some at the time suspecting that _____ had had him poisoned
Wars of the Roses.fact: Suffolk successfully negotiated the marriage to Henry of Margaret of Anjou, only a distant relation of Charles VII through marriage rather than blood, in exchange for the strategically important lands of Maine and Anjou. Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: During this time, _____ continued to suffer reversals in France
Wars of the Roses.fact: During this time, England continued to suffer reversals in France.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In _____, Suffolk was arrested, imprisoned in the Tower of London, and impeached in the Commons
Wars of the Roses.fact: In 1450, Suffolk was arrested, imprisoned in the Tower of London, and impeached in the Commons. Henry intervened and instead exiled Suffolk for five years, but en route to Calais, Suffolk was captured and executed on 2 May 1450.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry intervened and instead exiled Suffolk for five years, but en route to Calais, Suffolk was captured and executed on 2 May _____
Wars of the Roses.fact: In 1450, Suffolk was arrested, imprisoned in the Tower of London, and impeached in the Commons. Henry intervened and instead exiled Suffolk for five years, but en route to Calais, Suffolk was captured and executed on 2 May 1450.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Suffolk was succeeded by Edmund Beaufort, Duke of Somerset, nephew of Henry Beaufort, as the leader of the faction pursuing peace with France, who had been appointed as Richard's replacement as comman
Wars of the Roses.fact: Suffolk was succeeded by Edmund Beaufort, Duke of Somerset, nephew of Henry Beaufort, as the leader of the faction pursuing peace with France, who had been appointed as Richard's replacement as commander in France in 1448.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Somerset's political position was somewhat fragile, as English military failures in _____ following a resumption of hostilities left him vulnerable to criticism from Richard's allies at court
Wars of the Roses.fact: Somerset's political position was somewhat fragile, as English military failures in 1449 following a resumption of hostilities left him vulnerable to criticism from Richard's allies at court.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Somerset had by this time become a close ally of Henry's wife, _____ of Anjou
Wars of the Roses.fact: Somerset had by this time become a close ally of Henry's wife, Margaret of Anjou. Margaret herself wielded almost complete control over the pliable king Henry, and her close friendship with Somerset led many to suspect the two were having an affair; indeed, upon the birth of Henry and Margaret's son, Edward of Westminster in 1453, there were widespread rumours that Somerset was the father.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: On 15 April _____, the English suffered a major reversal in France at Formigny, which paved the way for the French reconquest of Normandy
Wars of the Roses.fact: On 15 April 1450, the English suffered a major reversal in France at Formigny, which paved the way for the French reconquest of Normandy.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The rebel manifesto, _____ of the Poor Commons of Kent, written under the stewardship of rebel leader Jack Cade, accused the crown of extortion, perversion of justice, and election fraud
Wars of the Roses.fact: The rebel manifesto, The Complaint of the Poor Commons of Kent, written under the stewardship of rebel leader Jack Cade, accused the crown of extortion, perversion of justice, and election fraud.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: The rebels occupied parts of _____, and executed James Fiennes, the unpopular Lord High Treasurer
Wars of the Roses.fact: The rebels occupied parts of London, and executed James Fiennes, the unpopular Lord High Treasurer. Richard of York used the opportunity to return from Ireland and went to London.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: They dispersed after they were supposedly pardoned but several ringleaders, including _____, were later executed
Wars of the Roses.fact: The rebel manifesto, The Complaint of the Poor Commons of Kent, written under the stewardship of rebel leader Jack Cade, accused the crown of extortion, perversion of justice, and election fraud. They dispersed after they were supposedly pardoned but several ringleaders, including Cade, were later executed.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: After the rebellion, the grievances of Cade and his followers formed the basis of _____ of York's opposition to a royal government from which he felt unduly excluded
Wars of the Roses.fact: After the rebellion, the grievances of Cade and his followers formed the basis of Richard of York's opposition to a royal government from which he felt unduly excluded. Richard of York used the opportunity to return from Ireland and went to London.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: By the summer of the latter year, _____ seemed to have lost the power struggle
Wars of the Roses.fact: After the rebellion, the grievances of Cade and his followers formed the basis of Richard of York's opposition to a royal government from which he felt unduly excluded. Richard of York used the opportunity to return from Ireland and went to London.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Richard of York used the opportunity to return from _____ and went to London
Wars of the Roses.fact: Richard of York used the opportunity to return from Ireland and went to London.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Angling himself as a reformer to demand better government, he was eventually imprisoned for much of _____ and 1453
Wars of the Roses.fact: Angling himself as a reformer to demand better government, he was eventually imprisoned for much of 1452 and 1453.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Throughout these quarrels, _____ himself had taken little part in proceedings
Wars of the Roses.fact: Throughout these quarrels, Henry himself had taken little part in proceedings. Henry was described as more interested in matters of religion and learning, which, coupled with his timid and passive nature and, if not well-intentioned, aversion to warfare, made him an ineffectual king for the time.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: He displayed several symptoms of mental illness, possibly inherited from his maternal grandfather, _____ VI of France
Wars of the Roses.fact: He displayed several symptoms of mental illness, possibly inherited from his maternal grandfather, Charles VI of France.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: His near-total lack of leadership in military matters had left the English forces in France scattered and weak, which left them ripe for defeat at Formigny in _____
Wars of the Roses.fact: His near-total lack of leadership in military matters had left the English forces in France scattered and weak, which left them ripe for defeat at Formigny in 1450.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Perhaps in reaction to the news, Henry suffered a complete mental breakdown, during which he failed to recognise his newborn son, _____
Wars of the Roses.fact: Perhaps in reaction to the news, Henry suffered a complete mental breakdown, during which he failed to recognise his newborn son, Edward.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: On 22 March _____, Cardinal John Kemp, the Lord Chancellor, died, and Henry could not be induced to nominate a successor, thus making government in the king's name constitutionally impossible
Wars of the Roses.fact: On 22 March 1454, Cardinal John Kemp, the Lord Chancellor, died, and Henry could not be induced to nominate a successor, thus making government in the king's name constitutionally impossible.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: To ensure the country could be governed, a Regency Council was established and, despite the protests of Margaret, was led by Richard of York, who was appointed Lord Protector and Chief Councillor on 2
Wars of the Roses.fact: On 22 March 1454, Cardinal John Kemp, the Lord Chancellor, died, and Henry could not be induced to nominate a successor, thus making government in the king's name constitutionally impossible. To ensure the country could be governed, a Regency Council was set up and, despite the protests of Margaret, was led by Richard of York, who was appointed Lord Protector and Chief Councillor on 27 March 1454.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: York appointed his brother-in-law, _____, Earl of Salisbury, to the post of Chancellor, backing the Nevilles against their chief adversary, Henry Percy, Earl of Northumberland
Wars of the Roses.fact: York appointed his brother-in-law, Richard Neville, Earl of Salisbury, to the post of Chancellor, backing the Nevilles against their chief adversary, Henry Percy, Earl of Northumberland. In backing the Nevilles, York gained a key ally, Salisbury's son Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick, one of the wealthiest and most powerful magnates in the kingdom.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In backing the _____, York gained a key ally, Salisbury's son Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick, one of the wealthiest and most powerful magnates in the kingdom
Wars of the Roses.fact: York appointed his brother-in-law, Richard Neville, Earl of Salisbury, to the post of Chancellor, backing the Nevilles against their chief adversary, Henry Percy, Earl of Northumberland. In backing the Nevilles, York gained a key ally, Salisbury's son Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick, one of the wealthiest and most powerful magnates in the kingdom.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: York removed _____ from his position and imprisoned him in the Tower of London
Wars of the Roses.fact: York removed Somerset from his position and imprisoned him in the Tower of London. Somerset was released and restored to favour, and York was forced out of court into exile.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: In _____, Henry made a surprise recovery from his mental instability, and reversed much of Richard of York's progress
Wars of the Roses.fact: In 1455, Henry made a surprise recovery from his mental instability, and reversed much of Richard of York's progress.

Wars of the Roses.fact: However, disaffected nobles, chiefly the Earl of Warwick and his father the Earl of Salisbury, backed the claims of the rival House of York to control of the government.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: Henry, _____, and a select council of nobles elected to hold a Great Council at Leicester on 22 May, away from Somerset's enemies in London
Wars of the Roses.fact: Somerset was released and restored to favour, and York was forced out of court into exile. Henry, Somerset, and a select council of nobles elected to hold a Great Council at Leicester on 22 May, away from Somerset's enemies in London.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology

Wars of the Roses.fact: Fearing that charges of treason would be brought against them, York and his allies gathered an army to intercept the royal party at St Albans, before they could reach the Council.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology

Wars of the Roses.fact: Though the ensuing struggle resulted in fewer than 160 casualties combined, it was a decisive Yorkist victory. With the king in his custody and many of his key rivals dead, York was again appointed Lord Protector by Parliament, and the Yorkist faction regained their position of influence.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology
Wars of the Roses.question: King Henry VI had been taken prisoner by _____'s men, who had found the monarch hiding in a local tanner's shop, abandoned by his courtiers and advisors
Wars of the Roses.fact: Fearing that charges of treason would be brought against them, York and his allies gathered an army to intercept the royal party at St Albans, before they could reach the Council. Though the ensuing struggle resulted in fewer than 160 casualties combined, it was a decisive Yorkist victory.

Wars of the Roses.subject: Environment & Ecology

Wars of the Roses.fact: With the king in his custody and many of his key rivals dead, York was again appointed Lord Protector by Parliament, and the Yorkist faction regained their position of influence.

Wetland.question: The convention works closely with five _____ (IOPs)
Wetland.fact: === Ramsar Convention === The Ramsar Convention (full title: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance, especially as Waterfowl Habitat), is an international treaty designed to address global concerns regarding wetland loss and degradation.  The primary purposes of the treaty are to list wetlands of international importance and to promote their wise use, with the ultimate goal of preserving the world's wetlands.  Methods include restricting access to some wetland areas, as well as educating the public to combat the misconception that wetlands are wastelands.  The convention works closely with five International Organisation Partners (IOPs).  These are: Birdlife International, the IUCN, the International Water Management Institute, Wetlands International and the World Wide Fund for Nature.  The partners provide technical expertise, help conduct or facilitate field studies and provide financial support.  == Restoration == Restoration and restoration ecologists intend to return wetlands to their natural trajectory by aiding directly with the natural processes of the ecosystem

Wetland.fact: As a result of peat drainage, the organic carbon that had built up over thousands of years and is normally under water is suddenly exposed to the air.  The peat decomposes and is converted into carbon dioxide (CO2), which is then released into the atmosphere.  Peat fires cause the same process to occur rapidly and in addition create enormous clouds of smoke that cross international borders, which now happens almost yearly in Southeast Asia.  While peatlands constitute only 3% of the world's land area, their degradation produces 7% of all CO2 emissions.  === Climate change mitigation === Studies have favorably identified the potential for coastal wetlands (also called blue carbon ecosystems) to provide some degree of climate change mitigation in two ways: by conservation, reducing the greenhouse gas emissions arising from the loss and degradation of such habitats, and by restoration, to increase carbon dioxide drawdown and its long-term storage.
